title: Tensor and adjunction compatibility of canonical ringed-topos path comparisons
statement:
Let $W,X_1,X_2,Y$ be topoi presented by sites small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings and morphisms of ringed topoi $f_i:W\to X_i$, $g_i:X_i\to Y$ for $i=1,2$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Fix an isomorphism $g_1f_1\cong g_2f_2$ of ringed-topos morphisms, compatible with the structural ring maps. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical derived pullback/direct-image adjunctions, and the tensor comparisons $t_h:Lh^*(K\otimes^L H)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*K\otimes^L Lh^*H$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Put $P_i=Lf_i^*Lg_i^*$ and $V_i=Rg_{i*}Rf_{i*}$, with the composite adjunction $P_i\dashv V_i$ and its counit $e_i$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Let $\theta:P_2\xrightarrow{\sim}P_1$ be the canonical comparison obtained from derived pullback composition and the specified ringed commutation isomorphism. Let $c:V_1\xrightarrow{\sim}V_2$ be the canonical comparison obtained from the direct-image composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and the same commutation isomorphism. Define
$$d_{i,K,H}=t_{f_i,Lg_i^*K,Lg_i^*H}\circ Lf_i^*(t_{g_i,K,H}):P_i(K\otimes^L H)\longrightarrow P_iK\otimes^L P_iH.$$
Then for all $K,H\in D(Y)$,
$$d_{1,K,H}\circ\theta_{K\otimes^L H}=(\theta_K\otimes^L\theta_H)\circ d_{2,K,H}.$$
Moreover $c$ is the conjugate of $\theta$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Explicitly, for all $Z\in D(W)$,
$$e_{2,Z}\circ P_2(c_Z)=e_{1,Z}\circ\theta_{V_1Z}:P_2V_1Z\longrightarrow Z.$$
No exactness of the underived module pullbacks is assumed.

proof.text: Use the factorization equation of Functor.leftDerivedNatTrans for the canonical pullback comparison. Transport it from the homotopy localization Qh to the complex localization Q using quotientCompQhIso. Expand the composite left counit and cancel the intermediate quotient comparison. This proves on every complex P the equation theta_QP followed by the two path-1 complex comparisons equals the two path-2 complex comparisons followed by Q of the specified ordinary module square. No invertibility of these complex comparisons is used.

Package both sides of the asserted tensor equation as natural transformations on D(Y) times D(Y). The injectivity of two-variable restriction from lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent proves their equality: quotientCompQhIso transports the representative calculation from Q to Qh. Evaluate at K,H and expand ringedPathTensorMap.

proof.text: View each edge complex counit as a TwoSquare from the termwise module adjunction to the specified derived adjunction. Its mate is exactly the edge right-derived unit: apply the canonicalAdjunction Hom normalization to the ordinary complex counit, whose transpose is identity, and use mateEquiv_counit. Paste two such squares. mateEquiv_hcomp identifies the mate of the path complex counit with ringedPathRightUnit. The ordinary complex-composition isomorphisms have identity components.

proof.text: The representative equation of step 1 is the equality between whiskering the second path square by the ordinary comparison and whiskering the first path square by theta. Apply conjugateEquiv_mateEquiv_vcomp and mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_vcomp, then step 3. This gives the right-derived unit factorization for the conjugate of theta. Check degreewise that conjugating the termwise ordinary module square is the termwise conjugate of the composite module adjunctions. By rightDerived_ext and rightDerivedNatTrans_app, the independently defined canonical direct-image comparison equals that conjugate. Apply conjugateEquiv_counit to obtain the displayed counit identity.
